summary: Cutting with a hollow tool, a spherical shell r 18.5 to 40 revolved a full turn from a half ring in XY about the X axis, removed an 8 mm block lying wholly in the hollow, and could not cut a 12 x 8 x 8 block from x = 8 to 20 crossing the inner sphere. The revolve swept the profile's two edges on the axis into zero-area faces joining the spheres at the poles, and the boolean took the tool's void shell as a body of its own. Geometry is the PR test's (the issue's two blocks, plus x = 8 to 50 through both spheres and a join); a last case builds the same shell as a difference of two spheres. Volumes: the block's part inside r = R over its 8 x 8 section is F(R), integrated in closed form (G below, so F = 4*G(4, 4)); cross-checked by Richardson-extrapolated midpoint quadrature (agrees to 3e-10) and against the PR's Simpson values. The half-ring profile's inner arc runs 0 to 180 degrees, against the loop's direction (arcs are counter-clockwise only). The tolerance is 0.01 mm^3, as in the other boolean cases.

cases.name: block_inside_hollow_cut
cases.note: #451 case 1: an 8 mm block centred on the origin (its corners at r 6.93, well inside r 18.5) cut by the revolved shell. The block never meets the shell, so it stays as it is; SolidCraft removed it entirely. Known upstream behaviour (WR-442): SMLib revolves this two-loop profile into two solid shells, not a solid with a void, so the Rust result matches the C++ one and not the expected values below.

volume.formula: 8^3: the block lies wholly in the hollow (max r = sqrt(48) < 18.5)

cases.name: block_crossing_inner_sphere_cut
cases.note: #451 case 2: a 12 x 8 x 8 block from x = 8 to 20 crossing the inner sphere through its pole (18.5, 0, 0) on the revolve axis, cut by the revolved shell. What remains is the block inside r 18.5, ending in a piece of the inner sphere; SolidCraft could not cut it. Known upstream behaviour (WR-442): SMLib revolves this two-loop profile into two solid shells, not a solid with a void, so the Rust result matches the C++ one and not the expected values below.

cases.name: block_crossing_both_spheres_cut
cases.note: The PR test's third cut: the block from x = 8 to 50 crosses both spheres through their poles (18.5, 0, 0) and (40, 0, 0). Two pieces remain, one in the hollow and one beyond r 40. Known upstream behaviour (WR-442): SMLib revolves this two-loop profile into two solid shells, not a solid with a void, so the Rust result matches the C++ one and not the expected values below.

cases.name: block_crossing_inner_sphere_join
cases.note: The PR test's join: the block from x = 8 to 20 joined with the revolved shell. The result is the shell with its hollow partly filled (still a void, so lumps are not checked). Known upstream behaviour (WR-442): SMLib revolves this two-loop profile into two solid shells, not a solid with a void, so the Rust result matches the C++ one and not the expected values below.

cases.name: block_crossing_inner_sphere_cut_by_sphere_difference
cases.note: Control: the same cut as block_crossing_inner_sphere_cut, with the shell built as a sphere r 40 minus a sphere r 18.5 instead of a revolve (no revolve poles; a tool with a curved void, which the PR's second fix covers).
